problem: The fan-out gloss is ambiguous and slightly self-contradictory. Section 1 calls fan-out "the number of units that unit feeds", while Q1 calls it "the number of units it feeds, equal to the current layer width". Under the first phrase a unit feeds the next layer (whose width is not known here); under the second it is the current layer width. A student can take the two halves as different quantities.
fix: Say it in one consistent way: "For the weight matrix of a layer, fan-in n_in is the width of the layer feeding it (number of inputs per unit) and fan-out n_out is the width of that layer itself (number of output units). Equivalently, each input connects to n_out output units." Use this same wording in Q1's answer.

problem: "It averages fan-in and fan-out" is inaccurate: 2/(n_in + n_out) is the harmonic mean of 1/n_in and 1/n_out, not an arithmetic average of the two fan counts. A student may plug (n_in + n_out)/2 into the wrong place later.
fix: "It combines fan-in and fan-out through the harmonic mean: Var(W) = 2/(n_in + n_out), which equals the harmonic mean of the two variances 1/n_in and 1/n_out."

problem: "The rules below keep variance near one through the stack" is misleading. Xavier and He keep the variance the same from layer to layer; that common value need not be one, because it starts from the scale of the input data.
fix: "The rules below keep the activation variance constant from layer to layer, so the signal neither shrinks nor blows up."
